You are fixing three bugs in the python-dateutil checkout at /dateutil. Make EXACTLY the edits below (use the edit_file tool with exact string matching; do not reformat anything else; do not touch any test file). Then run the test suite and report.

=== EDIT 1: /dateutil/dateutil/relativedelta.py ===
Find this exact block (around line 98-101):

        # Check for non-integer values in integer-only quantities
        if any(x is not None and x != int(x) for x in (years, months)):
            raise ValueError("Non-integer years and months are "
                             "ambiguous and not currently supported.")

Replace it with (keep the same indentation, 8 spaces, and add the coercion right after):

        # Check for non-integer values in integer-only quantities
        if any(x is not None and x != int(x) for x in (years, months)):
            raise ValueError("Non-integer years and months are "
                             "ambiguous and not currently supported.")

        # Whole-number floats (e.g. 1.0) are equivalent to integers, so they
        # are coerced here to keep the rest of the code integer-only.
        if years is not None:
            years = int(years)
        if months is not None:
            months = int(months)

Rationale: relativedelta(months=1.0) currently passes the integer check but stores a float, so datetime(2000,1,1)+relativedelta(months=1.0) crashes with TypeError: integer argument expected, got float. It must behave like months=1.

=== EDIT 2: /dateutil/dateutil/rrule.py (method rrule._iter) ===
Find this exact block (around line 797-799):

        total = 0
        count = self._count
        while True:

Replace it with:

        total = 0
        count = self._count
        if count == 0:
            # A count of zero means the rule generates no occurrences at all
            self._len = 0
            return
        while True:

Rationale: rrule(YEARLY, count=0, dtstart=...) must yield no occurrences and rr.count() must be 0. Currently count=0 is treated as "no count" and it yields 8003 dates.

=== EDIT 3: /dateutil/dateutil/rrule.py (method rrule.__str__) ===
(a) Find:

        if self._count:
            parts.append('COUNT=' + str(self._count))

Replace with:

        if self._count is not None:
            parts.append('COUNT=' + str(self._count))

(b) Find:

        output.append(';'.join(parts))
        return '\n'.join(output)

Replace with:

        output.append('RRULE:' + ';'.join(parts))
        return '\n'.join(output)

Rationale: str(rrule(...)) must produce 'DTSTART:19970902T090000\nRRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;COUNT=5' (the RRULE: property name was missing), and a count of 0 must round-trip as COUNT=0.

=== THEN VERIFY (report all output verbatim) ===
Run: cd /dateutil && python -c "import dateutil; print(dateutil.__file__)"
Run: cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test -q 2>&1 | tail -30
(If pytest is missing, run: cd /dateutil && python -m unittest discover -s dateutil/test -t . 2>&1 | tail -30)

  cd /dateutil && python -c "from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta; relativedelta(months=1.5)"   (must still raise ValueError)
  cd /dateutil && python -c "from datetime import datetime; from dateutil.rrule import rrule, YEARLY; rr=rrule(YEARLY, count=0, dtstart=datetime(1997,9,2,9,0)); print(rr.count()); print(list(rr))"
  cd /dateutil && python -c "from datetime import datetime; from dateutil.rrule import rrule, YEARLY; rule=rrule(YEARLY, count=5, dtstart=datetime(1997,9,2,9,0)); print(repr(str(rule)))"
  cd /dateutil && python -c "from dateutil.rrule import rrulestr; print(repr(str(rrulestr('DTSTART:19970902T090000\nRRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;COUNT=5'))))"

You are fixing ONE bug in /dateutil/dateutil/relativedelta.py (python-dateutil 2.6.0 checkout). Do NOT modify any file under /dateutil/dateutil/test/. Make the minimal fix, then run the full test suite and report.

BUG: absolute values that are explicitly zero are lost when two relativedelta objects are added:
    relativedelta() + relativedelta(day=0, hour=0)   -> relativedelta()      (expected relativedelta(day=0, hour=0))
    relativedelta(day=0, hour=0) + relativedelta()   -> relativedelta()      (expected relativedelta(day=0, hour=0))
Root cause: `relativedelta.__add__` combines the absolute fields with truthiness, e.g. `day=other.day or self.day`, so an explicit 0 is treated like None. Fix `__add__` so each absolute field is taken from `other` when it is not None, else from `self` (explicit None checks instead of `or`), i.e.:

                                 leapdays=other.leapdays or self.leapdays,
                                 year=(other.year if other.year is not None
                                       else self.year),
                                 month=(other.month if other.month is not None
                                        else self.month),
                                 day=(other.day if other.day is not None
                                      else self.day),
                                 weekday=(other.weekday if other.weekday is not None
                                          else self.weekday),
                                 hour=(other.hour if other.hour is not None
                                       else self.hour),
                                 minute=(other.minute if other.minute is not None
                                         else self.minute),
                                 second=(other.second if other.second is not None
                                         else self.second),
                                 microsecond=(other.microsecond if other.microsecond
                                              is not None else
                                              self.microsecond))

Apply the SAME kind of fix to `__sub__` (which currently uses `self.X or other.X`), i.e. take `self.X` when it is not None else `other.X`, using explicit `is not None` checks. Keep `leapdays` exactly as it is (`self.leapdays or other.leapdays`). Do not change any other method.

Verify (report exact output of each):
  python -c "from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta as rd; print(rd()+rd(day=0, hour=0)); print(rd(day=0, hour=0)+rd()); print(rd(day=0, hour=0)+rd(day=0, hour=0)); print(rd(day=0)==rd(day=0)); print(rd()+rd(day=5, hour=3)); print(rd(day=5)+rd(day=0))"
  python -c "from datetime import datetime; from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta as rd; print(datetime(2000,1,1)+rd(day=0)); print(datetime(2000,1,1)+rd(hour=0)); print(datetime(2000,1,1)+rd(months=1, day=15)); print(datetime(2000,1,1)+rd(day=0, hour=0))"
  python -c "from datetime import datetime; from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta as rd; print(rd(day=0)-rd()); print(rd()-rd(day=0)); print(rd(datetime(2000,3,5), datetime(1999,1,2))); print(rd(datetime(2000,1,1), datetime(1999,1,1)))"

THEN run the full suite: `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test -q 2>&1 | tail -20`. Baseline before your change is `1064 passed, 43 skipped` with ZERO failures; if your change causes ANY failure, adjust until green again (never edit tests).

Report: `cd /dateutil && git diff dateutil/relativedelta.py` verbatim, all command outputs, and the final pytest summary line.

You are fixing TWO bugs in the dateutil parser at /dateutil/dateutil/parser.py (python-dateutil 2.6.0 checkout). Do NOT modify any file under /dateutil/dateutil/test/. Make the MINIMAL fix for each bug. Then run the full test suite and report.

BUG A: `parse('2017-07-17 06:15:', fuzzy=True)` raises `IndexError: list index out of range`. Expected: `datetime(2017, 7, 17, 6, 15)` (trailing colon ignored).
Root cause (already diagnosed): in `_parse`, inside the number branch, the HH:MM[:SS[.ss]] case does:

                    elif i+1 < len_l and l[i] == ':':
                        # HH:MM[:SS[.ss]]
                        res.hour = int(value)
                        i += 1
                        value = float(l[i])
                        res.minute = int(value)

                        if value % 1:
                            res.second = int(60*(value % 1))

                        i += 1

                        if i < len_l and l[i] == ':':
                            res.second, res.microsecond = _parsems(l[i+1])
                            i += 2

When the string ends with ':' , `l[i] == ':'` is true but `l[i+1]` is out of range. Fix it by only reading `l[i+1]` when it exists, e.g.:

                        if i < len_l and l[i] == ':':
                            if i+1 < len_l:
                                res.second, res.microsecond = _parsems(l[i+1])
                            i += 2

Verify: `python -c "from dateutil.parser import parse; print(parse('2017-07-17 06:15:', fuzzy=True)); print(parse('2017-07-17 06:15:30:', fuzzy=True)); print(parse('06:15:', fuzzy=True)); print(parse('2017-07-17 06:15:30', fuzzy=True))"` -> should print 2017-07-17 06:15:00, 2017-07-17 06:15:30, today 06:15:00, 2017-07-17 06:15:30 (no exception).

BUG B: `parse("http://biz.yahoo.com/ipo/p/600221.html", fuzzy_with_tokens=True)` currently returns a datetime whose hour is 1 (the 'p' in the URL path is wrongly consumed as a PM marker) and the 'p' is missing from the skipped tokens. Expected exactly:
    (datetime(2060, 2, 21, 0, 0, 0), ('http://biz.yahoo.com/ipo/p/', '.html'))
Note the expected skipped-tokens string DOES contain the 'p' (i.e. the 'p' must be treated as ordinary skipped text, not as an AM/PM marker). Diagnose the real root cause by instrumenting (e.g. print `_timelex().tokenize(...)` tokens, and trace which branch consumes the 'p' token in `_parse`) - do not guess. Then make the minimal fix. Likely relevant code is the 'Check am/pm' block near the end of `_parse` (it already contains a `val_is_ampm` / `if fuzzy and res.ampm is not None` / `if res.hour is None: if fuzzy: val_is_ampm = False` guard) - find why the guard does not prevent the 'p' from being consumed here, and fix it so that an am/pm token with no preceding hour (or an out-of-range hour) is simply skipped as unrecognized text in fuzzy mode while still being included in the skipped tokens. Do NOT change non-fuzzy behavior.

Also check these must still hold after your fix (report exact outputs):
  python -c "from dateutil.parser import parse; print(parse('1am July 11, 1995', fuzzy_with_tokens=True)); print(parse('1:00pm', fuzzy=True)); print(parse('12 am', fuzzy=True)); print(parse('11pm', fuzzy=True)); print(parse('2017-07-17 06:15:30.5', fuzzy=True))"
  python -c "from dateutil.parser import parse; print(parse('July 11, 1995 1am', fuzzy=True)); print(parse('1995-07-11T01:00:00', fuzzy=True))"

THEN run the full suite: `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test -q 2>&1 | tail -20`. The baseline before your change is `1064 passed, 43 skipped` with ZERO failures - if your change causes ANY failure, adjust your fix until the suite is green again (do not edit tests).

Report: `cd /dateutil && git diff dateutil/parser.py` verbatim, the root cause you found for BUG B, all command outputs, and the final pytest summary line.
